title: Financing Class Placement and Reimbursing Elections — Department Rule
content:
**Scope.** This rule sets which financing class an account in the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts is placed in, how it moves between classes, and when a class change takes effect.

1. **New contributory employers.** A new contributory employer is placed in the construction class (Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate) when its NAICS code begins with the construction prefix, and in the standard class (Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate) otherwise. It pays the new employer rate of its class.
2. **Move to experience rating.** At each computation date, a new employer whose liability has run for the class's experience rating eligibility months moves to experience rating: to Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve when its reserve balance at the computation date is zero or more, and to Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve when that balance is below zero.
3. **Between the two reserve classes.** An experience-rated employer moves between the positive and deficit reserve classes on the same test at each computation date.
4. **Delinquent reporting.** An experience-rated employer with any quarterly report missing at the computation date is placed in Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate for the whole next rate year, whatever its reserve.
5. **Reimbursing elections.** A 501(c)(3) nonprofit or a governmental entity may instead elect reimbursing financing, either within the election window after its liability determination, or effective 1 January by filing at least the class's termination notice days before that date. The election stays in force for the class's minimum years. A return to contributory financing likewise starts on a 1 January after the termination notice.
6. **Security.** A nonprofit electing reimbursing financing must keep the security deposit or bond; a governmental entity needs none.
7. **No rate features for reimbursing employers.** Reimbursing employers have no rate, no reserve account and no voluntary contributions; these are features of contributory financing only.
8. **Effective date.** A class change takes effect on 1 January of the rate year it is made for, except a reimbursing election made within the election window, which takes effect from the start of liability.

**Reserve balance at the computation date** means the reserve credits booked on or before the computation date preceding the rate year, less the benefit charges and transfers out booked on or before that date.

## When each change takes effect

| Change | Takes effect |
|---|---|
| New employer to an experience-rated class | 1 January of the rate year it is made for |
| Positive reserve to deficit reserve, or the reverse | 1 January of the rate year it is made for |
| Placement in the delinquent reporting class | 1 January of the rate year it is made for, for the whole of that year |
| Reimbursing election within the election window | From the start of liability |
| Reimbursing election by advance filing | 1 January |
| Return from reimbursing to contributory | A 1 January after the termination notice |

**Hypothetical cases.**
- A standard-class employer liable since 1 July 2024 has 24 months of liability at the computation date of 30 June 2026, reaching the class's experience rating eligibility months of 24. Its reserve balance on that date is USD 3,150.00, which is zero or more, so it moves to the positive reserve class for the 2027 rate year, from 1 January 2027.
- An experience-rated employer with a reserve balance of USD 40,000.00 has one quarterly report missing on 30 June 2026. It is placed in the delinquent reporting class for all of 2027, whatever its reserve.
- A governmental entity elects reimbursing financing within the election window. The election takes effect from the start of its liability and requires no security.
